# Conceptual metaphor source domains in technical prose — facts

> Source-anchored units about Conceptual metaphor source domains in technical prose: 7 across 3 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Lakoff defines a conceptual metaphor as a systematic mapping from a source domain (e.g. journeys) to a target domain (e.g. love); the mapping licenses source-domain language and inference patterns for the target. (high confidence) — https://terpconnect.umd.edu/~israel/lakoff-ConTheorMetaphor.pdf · keywords: Conceptual metaphor source domains in technical prose · also: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.01029
- [statement] Source domains are typically more concrete than targets; ARGUMENT is understood via WAR, so 'attack' and 'win' apply to arguments. (high confidence) — https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.01029 · keywords: Conceptual metaphor source domains in technical prose · also: https://terpconnect.umd.edu/~israel/lakoff-ConTheorMetaphor.pdf
- [statement] Software-development prose draws on a small set of source domains: construction (building a house), agriculture (garden), skilled craft, and finance (technical debt with interest). (medium confidence) — https://www.nexapp.ca/en/blog/metaphors-in-software-development · keywords: Conceptual metaphor source domains in technical prose · also: https://terpconnect.umd.edu/~israel/lakoff-ConTheorMetaphor.pdf
- [statement] Each source-domain lexical item may or may not use the mapping; conventional words in the source domain are not always conventional in the target, so extending a metaphor with new source vocabulary is a novel act, not automatic. (medium confidence) — https://terpconnect.umd.edu/~israel/lakoff-ConTheorMetaphor.pdf · keywords: Conceptual metaphor source domains in technical prose · also: https://www.nexapp.ca/en/blog/metaphors-in-software-development
- [statement] A corpus study on Common Crawl (Aono et al., 2024) found verb metaphors take direct objects with lower concreteness, imageability and familiarity, and appear more in emotional, subjective sentences; this supports abstract-target claims but suggests technical, unemotional prose may use fewer live metaphors. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.01029 · keywords: Conceptual metaphor source domains in technical prose · also: https://terpconnect.umd.edu/~israel/lakoff-ConTheorMetaphor.pdf
- [statement] Overextending a source domain beyond the initial need creates false equivalences and limits reflection. (low confidence) — https://www.nexapp.ca/en/blog/metaphors-in-software-development · keywords: Conceptual metaphor source domains in technical prose
- [statement] Critics say conceptual metaphors are often set up from intuitive, unsystematic evidence, and corpus-based validation is limited. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.01029 · keywords: Conceptual metaphor source domains in technical prose
